title: Testing Fundamentals in TypeScript: Test Design, Fakes & Flaky Tests
concept: Choose the right test for each risk and write tests that find bugs instead of confirming happy paths: unit, integration and end-to-end tests, equivalence classes and boundaries, testable code with an injected clock, test doubles without over-mocking, fake repositories, deterministic and isolated tests, property-based tests with shrinking, contract tests and mutation testing, each taught from a bug in the progress service of a learning platform.
description: An intermediate course for developers who already write tests and want them to catch real bugs. Every lesson starts from an incident in the progress service of the CodeDev learning platform - a certificate refused to a learner at exactly 80%, a deadline test that fails after midnight, a pipeline that is red only on CI, a mock that kept passing while production broke - and fixes it with a better test design: choosing unit, integration or end-to-end tests, equivalence classes and boundary values, injecting the clock, stubs, fakes and spies, an in-memory repository instead of a database, isolation from shared state, property-based testing with seeded generators and shrinking, contract tests for the progress API and mutation testing to measure your tests. 11 lessons with quizzes on real test code and hands-on TypeScript challenges.
